summary: Suriname's eVisa service says visitors coming for tourism pay an Entry Fee online before travel instead of getting a visa — USD or EUR 50 for a single entry or 75 for multiple entries, plus a service fee, for stays of up to 90 days. CARICOM passport holders are excluded from the fee, and visitors from 21 countries, including India, South Africa and Nigeria, must obtain a visa before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Suriname?
faq.answer: Suriname's eVisa service says visitors coming for tourism pay the Entry Fee online before travel instead of getting a visa: USD or EUR 50 for a single entry, or 75 for up to five entries within three months, plus an 8 service fee, for stays of up to 90 days. CARICOM passport holders are excluded from the fee. Since 1 May 2023 visitors from 21 countries — including India, South Africa, Nigeria, Pakistan and Bangladesh — must obtain a visa before travel.

faq.question: What is the difference between the Entry Fee and a Surinamese visa?
faq.answer: Since 1 July 2022, visitors coming for tourism pay the Entry Fee instead of getting a visa. It is paid online and covers tourism and family visits of up to 90 days — one entry, or up to five within three months. A visa is needed for business trips, for leaving the airport while in transit, and by the 21 nationalities that are not eligible for the Entry Fee.

faq.question: Can I pay the Suriname Entry Fee on arrival?
faq.answer: No official source we could read says the Entry Fee can be paid on arrival. It is paid online through the official service and the voucher is emailed to you as a PDF.

faq.question: Do CARICOM citizens pay the Suriname Entry Fee?
faq.answer: No. Holders of passports from CARICOM countries are exempt from the Entry Fee and listed as visa-exempt. For Haiti, Suriname's eVisa service also states that direct flights from Haiti are not allowed and that the government will not issue visas to Haitian citizens.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Suriname?
faq.answer: WHO says proof of vaccination is required from travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or after more than 12 hours in transit at an airport in one, and that WHO recommends the vaccination for Suriname.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Suriname?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says that after 30 days in Suriname all foreigners must report within one week to the police Immigration Section to obtain an extension-of-stay stamp, and that anyone intending to stay more than 3 months must apply for an Authorization for Temporary Stay (MKV) from a Surinamese embassy before travelling.
